newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM shares dive as 1996 profits disappoint.
newsitem.headline: DSM shares dive as 1996 profits disappoint.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM indicated on Tuesday 1996 profits from normal operations would fall by a third to some 700 million guilders, pressured by spiralling raw materials costs.

"Higher feedstock costs -- which could not yet be compensated for by higher selling prices -- had a greater-than-expected effect on the result for the fourth quarter of 1996," DSM said in a brief statement.
"The net result from ordinary activities for 1996 will be at least 700 million guilders," it added, but gave no further details.
The news sent investors scurrying for cover, hacking 5.10 guilders off DSM shares to 175.50 guilders when the Amsterdam bourse opened. The shares later recovered slightly to trade at 175.90.
Sector peer Akzo slipped 1.70 guilders to 264.50 on the fall-out.

Analysts had been forecasting net profit from normal operations of around 750 million guilders compared with a year-earlier 1.073 billion guilders, saying DSM's bulk chemicals activities would pick up after a poor first half.
"I had anticipated feedstock costs would weigh less heavily then they have," said Robert Jan Stassen, chemicals analyst with Bangert, Pontier and Partners in Amsterdam.
"DSM raised (selling) prices in September, but ...feedstock prices (for oil-based bulk) chemicals, particularly naphtha (the main raw material for plastics), have continued to rise."
DSM is due to publish definitive figures for 1996 on February 25.
